subject: Business Models
title: FTX: Crypto Castle of Cards
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on FTX: Crypto Castle of Cards.

hook.text: FTX was valued at $32 billion. It collapsed in 48 hours when a balance sheet leaked showing a $6 billion hole.

buildup.text: Sam Bankman-Fried built FTX as a crypto exchange and used customer funds to prop up his trading firm, Alameda.

discovery.text: FTX lent $10 billion in customer deposits to Alameda. When crypto prices dropped, neither could pay customers back.

twist.text: FTX had no board, no accounting department, and used QuickBooks for a $32 billion company. Governance was nonexistent.

climax.text: Bankman-Fried was convicted of fraud and sentenced to 25 years. $8 billion in customer funds was gone.

punchline.text: $32B valuation, 48-hour collapse. They used QuickBooks. Governance matters.

quiz.question: What triggered FTX's 48-hour collapse?
options: A leaked balance sheet revealing a $6 billion shortfall

details.summary: FTX grew to the third-largest crypto exchange with a 32 billion dollar valuation before collapsing in days when it was revealed that customer funds had been secretly transferred to Alameda Research, a sister trading firm controlled by founder Sam Bankman-Fried.
details.whyItMatters: FTX demonstrated that even in new industries like crypto, basic financial controls matter. Mixing customer funds with proprietary trading is the oldest financial crime..
takeaways: Customer deposits were secretly transferred to fund risky proprietary trading
The exchange collapsed in days when a bank run revealed insufficient reserves
Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted of fraud and sentenced to 25 years in prison

faq.question: How did FTX's fraud work mechanically?
faq.answer: FTX customer deposits were transferred to Alameda Research through a secret backdoor in the exchange's code. Alameda used these funds for risky trades, venture investments, and lavish spending. When crypto prices dropped, Alameda could not return the funds.

faq.question: What triggered FTX's collapse?
faq.answer: CoinDesk reported that Alameda's balance sheet was largely composed of FTX's own FTT token. Binance CEO announced he would sell his FTT holdings. This triggered a bank run as customers rushed to withdraw funds that FTX no longer had, collapsing the exchange within a week.
